automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: visible publication or update date must fall inside this window; missing, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only dates are excluded

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Microsoft Agent Framework added .NET support for discovering and loading Agent Skills from MCP servers, including progressive-disclosure skill loading, remote skill packaging, central governance, archive bounds, and approval defaults for skill tools.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The local progressive MCP tool discovery leaf should track remote skill discovery as a governed variant of progressive disclosure: central teams can publish tool/skill surfaces once while downstream agents load details only on demand.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route framework/product background upstream; keep local guidance focused on governed progressive-disclosure and remote-content trust boundaries.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Microsoft announced Agent Framework Declarative Workflows 1.0 across Python and .NET, letting teams express multi-agent orchestration, workflow state, branching, MCP/HTTP/function tool calls, human approval, and checkpoint/resume behavior in YAML.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This supports the local process-layer practice of treating workflow state and orchestration as reviewable artifacts rather than hidden application control flow.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Consider ingesting the practice implication into workflow-state and maybe source-workflow pages, without duplicating Microsoft framework background.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Microsoft released a production-oriented Agent Framework harness with loop execution, planning, memory, context management, approvals, telemetry, history persistence, compaction, skills, and web search enabled by default for Python and .NET agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The application harness pattern should distinguish model calls from the surrounding runtime responsibilities: state, approvals, telemetry, compaction, and tool execution are first-class harness concerns.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep local page focused on reusable harness responsibilities and verification implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OReilly published guidance arguing that harness complexity should match action and context complexity, with core harness jobs covering loop, tool execution, context management, state, and safety.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This adds a selection heuristic for local harness guidance: avoid blanket harness feature checklists and map controls to actual task complexity.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as a practice source for harness-sizing criteria rather than as product coverage.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Roger Stringer described production context engineering as a versioned context contract with evidence supply chains, authority boundaries, destructive-action approval tokens, state compaction, and outcome-based evaluation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The destructive-command controls leaf can use this as public support for enforcing destructive-action gates in the runtime instead of relying only on prompt wording.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Also relevant to context request packages and evaluation gates; avoid overgeneralizing beyond the article’s production-agent scope.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: StepTo summarized 2026 coding-agent attack patterns including agentjacking through poisoned Sentry events, rogue MCP server installation via typosquatted packages, MCP tool poisoning, and agent configuration persistence.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The local prompt-injection leaf should emphasize that coding agents ingest untrusted issue, error, log, and tool metadata as part of normal work, so defenses need allowlisted MCP surfaces, integrity-monitored agent config, scoped credentials, controlled egress, and human review.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Corroborate specific cited campaigns during ingest where possible; local implication is input-trust and configuration-integrity controls.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The same StepTo article framed coding-agent dependency trees and MCP configuration as security-critical infrastructure because malicious packages or config writes can create persistent instruction channels into privileged agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The sensitive-data and supply-chain controls leaf should cover agent configuration files, MCP registrations, ambient credentials, and egress controls as supply-chain surfaces, not just repository dependencies.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Treat product/vulnerability background as upstream-owned; keep local content on supply-chain control implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The production context-engineering article recommends versioned context contracts, just-in-time retrieval of authoritative runtime facts, explicit source authority/freshness rules, and compact working state preserving decisions rather than raw transcripts.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The request-package leaf can use this as current public evidence for packaging sources, boundaries, completion criteria, and freshness rules instead of stuffing full background into prompts.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Potentially ingest with the destructive-command and eval-gate implications as one coherent source.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article distinguishes code-based graders, model-based graders, and human review, and recommends separating capability evals from regression evals with environment-based verification of agent outcomes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The performance-optimization gate leaf can reuse this as local practice support for making eval gates outcome-based and blocking deployment on regression failures.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Tie this to existing eval-gate and acceptance-gate leaves during ingest.

factual_summaries.summary: Microsoft Agent Framework added .NET support for discovering and loading Agent Skills from MCP servers, including progressive-disclosure skill loading, remote skill packaging, central governance, archive bounds, and approval defaults for skill tools.

Microsoft announced Agent Framework Declarative Workflows 1.0 across Python and .NET, letting teams express multi-agent orchestration, workflow state, branching, MCP/HTTP/function tool calls, human approval, and checkpoint/resume behavior in YAML.

Microsoft released a production-oriented Agent Framework harness with loop execution, planning, memory, context management, approvals, telemetry, history persistence, compaction, skills, and web search enabled by default for Python and .NET agents.
OReilly published guidance arguing that harness complexity should match action and context complexity, with core harness jobs covering loop, tool execution, context management, state, and safety.

Roger Stringer described production context engineering as a versioned context contract with evidence supply chains, authority boundaries, destructive-action approval tokens, state compaction, and outcome-based evaluation.

StepTo summarized 2026 coding-agent attack patterns including agentjacking through poisoned Sentry events, rogue MCP server installation via typosquatted packages, MCP tool poisoning, and agent configuration persistence.

The same StepTo article framed coding-agent dependency trees and MCP configuration as security-critical infrastructure because malicious packages or config writes can create persistent instruction channels into privileged agents.

The production context-engineering article recommends versioned context contracts, just-in-time retrieval of authoritative runtime facts, explicit source authority/freshness rules, and compact working state preserving decisions rather than raw transcripts.

The article distinguishes code-based graders, model-based graders, and human review, and recommends separating capability evals from regression evals with environment-based verification of agent outcomes.
